lines.en: I swim slowly, but my teeth are dense.
The trench is black; I follow my lateral line.
My mouth will not close; my teeth show.
I creep forward along the trench floor.
Ignore the teeth; I am really quite small.
Cold water pushes me; I go with it.

lines.zh: 我绕开大鱼留下的水痕。
lines.en: I avoid the wake a big fish left behind.
Two hearts; I swim with great care.
My body is short, so I turn quickly.
My teeth are more noticeable than my body.
I swim toward the darker trench floor.
One flick and I slip into a rock crevice.
The current carries a smell of blood.
I swim past a crowd of glowing shrimp.

lines.zh: 我沿着沟壁横着挪，躲开强流。
lines.en: I crab along the trench wall, dodging the strong current.

lines.zh: 上面有影子掠过，我贴紧石头。
lines.en: A shadow passes overhead. I press to the stone.

lines.zh: 我张嘴换水，牙也跟着晃。
lines.en: I open my mouth to breathe, and the teeth sway.

lines.zh: 越往下越黑，我反倒安心。
lines.en: Darker as I go deeper. That settles me.
My mouth hangs open, waiting for something.
There is no sound at the bottom of the trench.
I hang still, teeth pointed forward.
Something moved in the dark just now.
I close my mouth slowly, then open it.
Both my hearts were nearly lost before.

lines.zh: 我在等一条倒霉的小鱼。
lines.en: I wait for one unlucky little fish.
The moss on the trench wall sways.
The pressure presses on my eyes.
Something just sank down from above.
I stay still; so do my teeth.
Hunger is harder to bear than darkness.
I hear fish swimming somewhere above me.
The trench floor is quiet as a grave.
What brings you down this deep?
Your lamp is brighter than my teeth.

lines.zh: 我从没见过这么大的东西。
lines.en: I have never seen anything this big.
Your fingers look soft enough to bite.
No nets; my teeth would snag them.

lines.zh: 我在你护目镜里看见自己。
lines.en: I see myself in your diving goggles.
You move, and I back away.
Are you a fish or a lump of iron?
Your bubbles scared the small fish off.
The light in this trench is mine.
One of my fangs has broken off.
Blood seeps out from behind my gills.
I only have two hearts to begin with.
I shrink into the crevice and tremble.
That hit left my head spinning.
A gash has opened along my side.
My teeth are intact; I can still bite.
I swim in a crooked, wobbling line.
The pain makes every scale stand up.
One more hit and I am gone.
That is the smell of meat, is it not?
What is that you are holding?
It has been a long time since I ate.
My teeth move before my brain does.
Drop it down; do not reach for me.
The scent comes drifting down the water.
I approach with my mouth already open.
A little closer and I can bite it.
This smell makes me forget the bigger fish.
I have followed this scent a long way.
You knocked out one of my teeth.
I am small; do not bump into me.
You pushed me into the rock crevice.
When the current swirls, I panic.
Two hearts do not survive many shoves.
I open my mouth to try to scare you.
Your boot kicked up a cloud of sand.
I slid away along the trench wall.
Do not crowd me; this place is narrow.
My head spins and my teeth will not close.
A mate comes near; I show my teeth first.
Two small heads come close together.
We circle slowly along the trench wall.
Her teeth are even longer than mine.
Do not interrupt; we are pairing up.
It is dark enough and quiet enough here.
I touched her with my tail fin.

lines.zh: 以后小鱼会藏在石缝里。
lines.en: Our little ones will hide in the crevices.
Even in the deep sea, one finds company.
We sink down, one after the other.
Is this thing that fell down edible?
I bite it and shake it twice.
Too hard; my teeth are nearly breaking.
I tuck it away beside my gills.
This is mine; nobody else may have it.
I drag it along for a short distance.
It weighs more than I do.
I set it down at the mouth of the crevice.
Bits of it are stuck between my teeth.
I will keep it and bite it when hungry.
That small fish has not noticed me.
It is half my size.
A glint of scales flickers in the dark.
The shadow on the trench floor shifts.

lines.zh: 我顺着沟壁绕到它尾后。
lines.en: I slip along the trench wall behind its tail.
My teeth show, and it starts to panic.
There is always food somewhere in this trench.
I lock onto that flicker of silver.
A shrimp counts as prey as well.
I flatten myself and stop moving.
It turns; I turn at the same time.
I chase it with my mouth wide open.
Water sprays around its little fins.
One more stroke and I bite.
It swims upward; I follow close behind.
My teeth are bigger than its body.
Do not hide behind that stone.
My tail slaps the trench wall loudly.
A big shadow passes overhead.
Hurry; do not let it get away.
I bit it, and now my teeth are stuck.
It thrashes wildly inside my mouth.
I shake my head and tear it apart.
Blood stains the water black.
My teeth are too long to close properly.
My bite punches straight through the scales.
A big fish smells blood; I must go.
I swallow slowly; my teeth get in the way.
The fight is over; I hide in a crevice.
I am not vicious; I just hate being hungry.
Deep in the trench, I open my eyes.
One of my own kind lies beside me.
It is too dark to see the trench wall.
My teeth were already full-grown at birth.
Cold water runs across my gills.
I huddle on the trench floor, still.
Many shadows swim past above me.
First I find a crevice to hide in.
The start of a life with two hearts.
The trench floor is quiet; good for ambush.
The water heats up; I dive deeper.
Lifted out of water, the air burns my gills.

lines.zh: 离开水，张着嘴也吸不到。
lines.en: Out of water, my open mouth draws nothing.
A muffled blast underwater flips me over.
Something punched straight through my fin.
This light makes my teeth tingle.
Every small fish in the trench is gone.
Lightning enters the water; my whole body jerks.
Below is no water, only blackness.
